verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents concurrency keys that create per-user queue logic and per-queue concurrency limits. This covers part of the tenant-isolation and fairness side of the story rather than a single FIFO queue. Nothing in the evidence shows assigning priorities to runs or an explicit fair-scheduling algorithm across tenants. Missing for 10: run-level priority assignment, documented fair-scheduling semantics across tenants, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I assign priorities to runs and get fair scheduling across tenants instead of a single FIFO queue

citations.quote: With concurrency keys you can create bespoke queue logic for each of your users.
You can set the concurrency limit for a task by setting the `concurrencyLimit` property on the task's queue. This limits the number of runs that can be executing at any one time
